speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with a headache and worsening vision over three weeks; to begin my evaluation, are you experiencing any visual disturbances like halos, double vision, or blind spots, and has your headache severity changed with eye movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System (PACNS). The patient is a 69-year-old female with a 3-week history of headache and progressive vision loss, without fever or systemic symptoms, which is highly suggestive of an isolated inflammatory vasculopathy of the brain. I recommend immediate MRI of the brain with contrast and lumbar puncture for cerebrospinal fluid analysis to confirm the diagnosis.
